summary: Intermittent OOMs on Dedicated L40S pool during burst traffic (suspected profile KV-cache headroom / concurrency defaults)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent OOMs on their Dedicated L40S pool under bursty traffic (short time window of high concurrency). Failures present as 5xx with "CUDA out of memory" in runtime logs; service recovers after a few minutes but repeats during spikes.

Impact
- Elevated error rate (up to ~1.2% of requests during spikes) and latency increases (queueing) when runtime retries / backpressure kicks in.
- Customer has a nightly batch job + daytime interactive traffic; OOMs occur when the batch job overlaps with interactive surge.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Dedicated
- Hardware: L40S pool (PCIe)
- Region: us-west
- Runtime version: runtime-1.21.3 (customer report) with profile pack enabled (default profile selection)
- Profiles: L40S default profile (customer did not pin a profile_version)

Customer symptoms / error message
- Runtime log excerpt (from customer bundle):
  - "CUDA error: out of memory" during prefill
  - "allocator: unable to reserve block" followed by model worker restart
- Customer notes: OOMs more frequent when prompt lengths are mixed (many small chats + occasional long-context requests).

Steps to reproduce (best effort)
1) Load llama-3.1-70b-instruct on L40S pool
2) Send mixed workload: 70% short prompts (<= 512 input tokens, <= 256 output), 30% long prompts (>= 8k input tokens, 256-512 output)
3) Burst concurrency from ~40 -> ~90 within ~30s
4) Observe GPU memory climbing to near full and then abrupt OOM during a prefill wave

Support asks
- Confirm whether this is a known L40S profile issue.
- Provide safe workaround (configuration) the customer can apply immediately.
- Provide ETA for a durable fix / updated profile defaults.

Attachments
- Customer provided: runtime debug bundle + ~15 minutes of logs around 2026-01-23T19:10Z (stored in Support drive; link shared in internal comment).
investigation_notes:
Triage notes (Support + Runtime)
- Pattern matches memory headroom exhaustion under bursty prefill when batching + concurrency pushes KV cache + activations near device limit.
- L40S is more sensitive than H100 to fragmentation and transient peaks during mixed prompt lengths; we’ve previously discussed raising KV cache headroom / lowering default concurrency for L40S.

Internal observations
- From customer log timestamps, OOM occurs shortly after a spike in admitted requests (likely scheduler queue + prefill concurrency wave).
- OOMs correlate with a brief rise in "scheduler_queue_ms" and then sudden worker restart.

Hypothesis
1) L40S default profile has insufficient memory headroom for bursty mixed workloads (KV cache reservation + allocator fragmentation + prefill peak).
2) Admission control thresholds for L40S may be too permissive when multiple long-context prefills arrive together.

What we asked the customer for
- Confirmation of: max context window, typical prompt length distribution, and whether they’re using streaming.
- Their current configured concurrency caps (if any) and whether they have request-level timeouts.

What we checked internally
- Reviewed recent L40S stability discussions: headroom defaults were intentionally aggressive for throughput and may need adjustment for Dedicated workloads with burstiness.
- Noted an in-flight runtime change to adjust L40S KV cache headroom settings and guardrails.

Risk assessment
- Workaround should prioritize stability over absolute throughput (customer prefers no 5xx).
workaround:
Recommended immediate workaround (customer-approved)
1) Cap concurrency on the Dedicated route for L40S pool:
   - Set max_concurrency to 64 (previous observed burst ~90)
   - If still seeing OOM, reduce to 56
2) Reduce maximum prefill batch pressure:
   - Lower max_batch_tokens / max_prefill_tokens_per_batch (exact field names vary by install; Support provided the applicable config snippet for Dedicated control plane)
3) Increase memory headroom / reduce KV cache target:
   - Increase kv_cache_headroom_percent (or equivalent) by +4-6% on L40S
4) For long-context traffic, recommend routing to a separate pool (if feasible) or using request-level limits:
   - Enforce max_input_tokens for the interactive endpoint during batch overlap windows

Customer notes on workaround
- Customer applied concurrency cap at 64 and reported OOMs stopped for 48 hours (throughput reduced ~8-12% during spikes but acceptable).
resolution:
Resolved as: Mitigated via configuration workaround; durable fix tracked to updated L40S profile defaults.

Outcome
- Customer confirmed stability after applying concurrency cap + increased headroom.
- Runtime team confirmed this aligns with planned L40S profile adjustment (raise KV cache headroom / tighten default concurrency and admission control for bursty mixed workloads).

Customer communication
- We explained this is not a model bug; it’s an interaction between burst admission + L40S memory limits and current profile defaults.
- We offered to help them pin a known-good profile version once the updated profile pack ships, and to proactively notify before enabling any new default profile changes on their Dedicated deployment.
next_steps:
Follow-ups
- Runtime: adjust L40S profile defaults for memory headroom and/or admission control thresholds; ensure change is clearly documented in L40S expected behavior.
- SRE: add alerting guidance for L40S OOM early signals (fragmentation/compaction time, near-OOM watermark) and confirm rollback/kill-switch behavior for profile changes.
- Support: add a canned workaround snippet for L40S burst OOMs in the internal playbook; include when to recommend pool split by context length.

Open questions
- Whether customer should separate long-context workloads into a dedicated route/pool (recommended) vs rely on global caps.
- Whether customer wants to pin profile_version once available (likely yes).
